testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed as far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Heavy cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip:

options.text: No part of your vehicle should be visible in any mirror.
Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: When properly adjusted, your mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your own vehicle gives you a reference point to judge where other objects are.

questions.question: Drivers trapped behind a slow-moving vehicle often:

options.text: Allow the vehicle plenty of space.
Are happy with the speed of travel.

questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If you are being tailgated, let the other driver pass.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
A message may be upsetting to the driver.
People like to read and may become too engaged in their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it takes your mind off the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must be equipped with:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must be equipped with anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Without a working ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as usual. Get your ABS serviced as soon as possible.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Move straight forward, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then move forward to the left.
Move straight forward, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move straight forward, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, move straight forward first. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What task may a CDL applicant be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you may need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: What is a danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.explanation: Swerving can sometimes help avoid a hazard, but it is risky. Large trucks and tractors with multiple trailers can flip over when swerving.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the brake system. Have a mechanic check it right away.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
To allow for a change in pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil. These build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks daily at the end of your driving shift.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: After driving down a steep grade, your brakes may be very hot. Do not use the parking brake until the brakes cool down. Using it while hot can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When asked to change lanes during the on-road driving test, check traffic carefully. Use the proper turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about a cardboard box on the roadway?

options.text: You should expect to see it on the roadway.
It is usually empty and safe.
It could contain something heavy that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could contain something heavy that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. Even a cardboard box could hide a heavy or hard object that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking your windshield before a trip, which task should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wiper arm spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks or damage that blocks your view. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the blades for damage, stiff rubber, and loose attachment. Do not remove and sharpen the wiper blades.

questions.question: When inspecting your tires, which condition is NOT acceptable?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires must be the same size.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums must not have cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before every trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: When accelerating on wet or slippery roads, a driver should:

options.text: Not be concerned about the pavement.

questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly on roads with poor traction.

questions.question: If your driving privilege is disqualified:

options.text: Your employer will be notified by the state.
You must notify your employer within two business days.
You must notify your employer within a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must notify your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you are disqualified from driving.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: You should not be concerned with other motorists.
You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
You should change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, check traffic, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: A one-way check valve:

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing:

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct procedures at a simulated location.

questions.question: Cargo being transported should be checked:

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. Also check cargo each time you stop. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured during the entire trip.

questions.question: While driving, gauges should be:
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges while driving for any signs of problems. Check that gauges work properly before starting your trip.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded on a truck?

options.text: The person who loaded the truck

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for cargo even if someone else loaded it. The driver must inspect the cargo and make sure it is properly secured.

questions.question: A jogger wearing a stereo headset:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Can hear the sounds of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle and may do dangerous things because they don't know you are there.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Check how tight the belt is and make sure it is in good condition.

questions.question: When starting an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Check your truck's gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are angry.
Warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Your horn is used to warn others of your presence. Use it only when necessary because it may startle other drivers and cause danger.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only at the beginning of a drive.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Inspect cargo and securing devices before starting a trip. During a trip, check the load within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, air storage tanks hold compressed air for the brakes. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes is ____ in a minute.
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not be more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle because repairs are needed.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A vehicle with dual parking control valves has a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they are activated due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance is:

options.text: Longer than on a normal driving surface.
Shorter than on a normal driving surface.
About the same as on a normal driving surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than on a normal driving surface.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. This is because your tires have less grip on the road.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right before turning left. Always start your left turn from the right lane when two left turn lanes are available.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Driving tired is dangerous. Do not rely on caffeine to stay awake.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you apply spring brakes slowly. A lever on the dashboard controls the valve in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: Slower than the traffic around you.
The same speed as the traffic around you.
Faster than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, both systems share:
questions.explanation: Both brake systems share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a trailer is challenging because:

options.text: It should be avoided in summer months.
Animals are attracted to the smell.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and the meat swings, which makes the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to reach 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are on the wheels and axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Cargo should be covered to:
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.
